index.features.title: Everything a Minecraft server needs to run for real
index.features.lead: No duct tape: an optimized server, a panel to configure it without editing files, backups that leave the machine and clear ways to open it to the internet.
index.f1.title: Optimized server
index.f1.text: Paper 26.2 by default, or Purpur, Fabric, NeoForge and Vanilla. Java 25, Aikar flags and performance patches.
index.f2.title: Its own web panel
index.f2.text: Plain language, no jargon, in English, Portuguese or Spanish: server status, players, game rules, settings, Modrinth plugins and backups, with alerts that tell you what to do.
index.f3.title: Encrypted backups
index.f3.text: Incremental, deduplicated restic, scheduled or on demand, with a safe restore that rolls back if something fails.
index.f4.title: Bedrock crossplay
index.f4.text: Geyser and Floodgate behind one toggle: phone, console and Windows players join without a Java account.
index.f5.title: Nobody takes your name
index.f5.text: Each player creates a password in a window inside the game, with no plugin or mod, on Paper, Vanilla, Fabric and NeoForge. The panel stays on your machine, with Docker behind a proxy that can't create containers.
index.f6.title: Runs anywhere
index.f6.text: Home PC, VPS or EasyPanel. Port forwarding, a playit.gg tunnel for CGNAT or a VPS as a bridge.
index.start.title: Your Minecraft server online in a few minutes
index.start.leadHtml: All you need is Docker with Compose v2, make and openssl. Set aside at least 6 GB of RAM.
index.backups.title: World backups stored off the machine
index.backups.lead: Each copy sends only what changed and is encrypted before it leaves. Saving pauses during the copy, so nothing is left half-written. You choose the destination right in the panel, with a connection test.
index.panel.title: A Minecraft server panel that looks like Minecraft
index.panel.lead: Square corners, beveled buttons, pixel font and icons. Every part of the server has its own page.

index.faq.title: Common questions before starting your server
index.faq.a1: A project to run a Minecraft server on Docker, organized for real use: an optimized server, a friendly web panel, encrypted backups and guides to go live at home, on a VPS or on EasyPanel.
index.faq.q2: How do I create a Minecraft server with Minetune?
index.faq.a2: With Docker installed, clone the repository and run make init to generate the passwords and make up to start everything. The panel opens at localhost:8080 and the game at localhost:25565.
index.faq.a2Html: With Docker installed, clone the repository and run make init to generate the passwords and make up to start everything. The panel opens at localhost:8080 and the game at localhost:25565.
index.faq.q3: Which server types and versions are supported?
index.faq.a3: Paper (default), Purpur, Fabric, NeoForge and Vanilla. The panel lists the official versions of each one, newest first, and warns you when an old version needs a different Java image.
index.faq.a4: On the local disk by default, or off the machine on Cloudflare R2, Amazon S3 or your own S3 such as RustFS. Backups are incremental and encrypted with restic, and you set the destination in the panel with a connection test.
index.faq.q5: Can people play from a phone or console?
index.faq.a5: Yes. Turn on Bedrock crossplay in the settings and Minetune installs Geyser and Floodgate, so phone, console and Windows players join on port 19132 without a Java account.
index.faq.q6: Do I need to open ports on my router?
index.faq.a6: Not necessarily. With a public IP you can use port forwarding; without one, or behind CGNAT, the playit.gg tunnel works with no open ports. You can also use a VPS as a bridge or host on EasyPanel.
index.faq.q7: How many players can the server handle?
index.faq.a7: The player limit is a panel setting, from 1 to 1000. The real limit is the machine: CPU, memory and internet. Dozens of players fit on a regular machine; hundreds need a strong machine and usually several servers behind a proxy.

mapa.title: Minecraft seed map: biomes and structures — Minetune
mapa.description: See the biomes, villages, strongholds and spawn of any Minecraft Java 26.2, 26.1 and 1.21 seed, right in your browser.
mapa.ogTitle: Minecraft seed map: biomes and structures
mapa.ogDescription: Biomes, villages, strongholds and spawn for any Minecraft Java seed, computed in your browser.
mapa.ldDescription: Shows the biomes, structures and spawn of a Minecraft Java seed, computed in the browser.
mapa.lead: Enter a seed and see where the biomes, villages, strongholds and spawn are. Click a spot or a structure to copy the teleport command. Everything is computed in your browser, with the same math the game uses to generate the world.
mapa.canvas: Seed biome map. Drag to move and use the mouse wheel or the buttons to zoom in.
mapa.note1.title: Where do I find my server's seed?
mapa.note1.html: In game, type /seed (you need to be an operator). In Minetune, open the panel Console and run seed.
mapa.note2.title: Is the map accurate?
mapa.note2.text: Biomes and structure positions follow the game's generation. Desert and jungle temples may not appear when the terrain doesn't allow it, and the map doesn't know what has already been built or destroyed in your world.
mapa.note3.title: Where does the math come from?
mapa.note3.html: From the cubiomes library, with 26.x support from xpple's fork, both MIT licensed. Nothing is sent to any server.
